metadata.notes: Added 2026-08-17, closing ROADMAP.md's own long-named gap ('the real alkaline (baking-soda) parboil-roughening technique... remain open,' first flagged 2026-08-13) — this repo's first entity whose real culinary role here is a CHEMICAL PROCESS AID, not a flavor/seasoning ingredient (isAlkalizingAgent is deliberately NOT isSeasoning/isSeasonable — raising the parboiling water's pH to break down potato surface starch/pectin is not a taste contribution, the same 'a genuinely new concept SALT's isSeasoning/isSeasonable capabilities don't fit' reasoning egg.json's own crackContainmentNote already established for salt-in-boiling-water). Deliberately does NOT model baking soda's other, more common real culinary role — a leavening agent in actual baking (reacting with an acid to release CO2) — no LEAVEN/bread-shaped verb exists in this vocabulary yet; only the alkaline-parboil role is wired.
metadata.alkalizationNote: The real mechanism, cited in data/actions/alkaline_parboil.json's own safetyNote-equivalent: raising water pH accelerates pectin demethylation/solubilization at the potato surface (the same cell-wall-softening chemistry fry.json's agitationNote already cites Binner, Jardine & Renard 2000 for, here deliberately accelerated rather than a side effect to manage) — corroding a rough, starchy surface layer that then blisters and crisps dramatically under high roasting heat. See alkaline_parboil.json for the full citation.
